words.trans: n. 铅球运动员
examples: He let out a roar like a shot-putter.
The shot-putter stepped into the circle and wound up.

words.trans: adj. 大口吞咽的；咕嘟吞咽的
examples: The water just made a gulping sound.
He drank the tea in one long gulping swallow.

words.trans: v.（用全身力气）猛扔、猛甩；用力举起重物抛出
examples: He heaved the rock as far as he could.
They heaved the heavy crate onto the truck.

words.trans: adj. 紧张不安的；心神不宁的；神经紧绷的
examples: His muscles ached from working tense and jittery.
Too much coffee makes me feel jittery.

words.word: have something to show for it
words.trans: 忙活之后拿得出手的成果、收获。潜台词：付出了大量辛苦，期待更好回报，但现实结果却糟糕、很不值
examples: All he had to show for it was the power to prick someone.
I worked all summer but had nothing to show for it.

words.trans: 1.弄到、设法搞到（物品、材料）——不是随手能拿到，需想办法费周折  2.抓住、逮住某人；握住
examples: Unless he could get hold of some anaesthetic.
Can you get hold of a spare key?

words.trans: v. 随水流漂浮、顺流漂行；乘筏漂流  n. 木筏，筏子
examples: Weightless insects rafted across the current.
They rafted down the river on logs.

words.trans: adj. 令人难以置信的；烧脑的；大到/怪到让人脑子转不过来的
examples: The mind-boggling power of the river.
The numbers involved are mind-boggling.

words.trans: 脑子都懵了，简直匪夷所思。核心：外界事物太离奇、太复杂、超出常规，让我感到震惊、无法理解，主语心智被外来信息冲击，不是自己累、分心
examples: My mind boggles at the money they spent.
It makes your mind boggle how anyone could believe that.

words.trans: v. 雕刻；刻凿；深深留下印记
examples: The river had engraved its course in the valley.
He engraved his initials on the ring.

words.trans: n.（水流的）路径、走向；河道；进程
examples: The water that had engraved its course.
The river changed course after the flood.

words.trans: （水流长年冲刷）刻凿出它的河道，冲刷雕琢出水流行进的路径
examples: The stream slowly engraved its course.
Over time the river engraves its course.

words.trans: adj. 巨大的；无比强烈的；浩瀚的
examples: This moment seemed so immense right now.
An immense crowd filled the square.

words.trans: 持续地、反复用鼻子嗅，发出呼哧的声响（持续动作，常用来写狗）
examples: He felt Archie snuffling around his feet.
The dog snuffled at the door.

words.trans: v. 悬垂，晃来晃去地吊着；垂在那里来回摇摆
examples: She was dangling her feet in the water.
He dangled the keys in front of the child.

words.trans: adj.（人的面部、神情）冷峻的，面无表情、神色强硬
examples: She glanced over, and her face was hard.
He gave me a hard stare.

words.trans: n. 一大口（饮品）  v. 大口猛喝
examples: He was about to take a swig of coffee.
He took a swig of water and kept running.

words.trans: adj. 零散的，临时的，非固定的
examples: He works as a handyman, doing odd jobs.
I picked up a few odd jobs.

words.trans: 固定复数短语：零活、杂活、临时零碎差事（描述手工、维修、体力零碎活）
examples: He was doing odd jobs, fixing things.
She does odd jobs to earn cash.

words.trans: adj. 井然有序的；收拾妥当、状态完好（不只是整洁，还包含设备完好、一切正常可用，随时待命）
examples: Keeping things shipshape is what he calls it.
He liked everything shipshape.

words.trans: 万事妥当（shipshape and Bristol fashion，布里斯托尔是英国老牌大港）
examples: He left the boat shipshape and Bristol fashion.
By midnight the kitchen was shipshape and Bristol fashion.

words.trans: 流言传开、消息四处流传
examples: Somehow a rumour got round about me.
Word soon got round that the factory was closing.

words.trans: 一丛
examples: He was watching a clump of dried grasses.
A clump of trees marked the bend.

words.trans: 有一天午饭的时候。英式小说、口语里非常地道，名词短语直接作时间状语，不需要介词（in/on）
examples: Jim came in one lunchtime and found me.
One lunchtime she walked out and never came back.

words.trans: n. 土匪，强盗，歹徒（多指结伙、在偏远地区劫掠的人）
examples: Some bandits broke into their house.
The bandits fled into the hills.

words.trans: v. 洗劫；翻箱倒柜大肆搜寻
examples: They ransacked the place.
The thieves ransacked the house.

words.trans: 1.（警方）搜捕、围捕、捉拿（嫌疑人、匪徒）  2.普通场景把人/动物聚拢、召集到一块儿
examples: The police rounded some of them up.
He rounded up all the children.

words.trans: adj.（景色）单调乏味的，灰暗没有生机；暗淡
examples: The landscape below was dull and flat.
a dull, overcast day.

words.trans: adj. 地势平坦，没有起伏
examples: The landscape was dull and flat.
The land is flat for miles.

words.trans: 固定习语：对……着迷、上头、上瘾
examples: I could get hooked on this!
He got hooked on collecting stamps.

words.trans: v. 细细地流淌；一滴滴缓缓往下流
examples: Sweat trickled down his neck.
Water trickled from the tap.

words.trans: adj. 痛苦的；煎熬的；万分紧张焦灼的
examples: They held the drones, agonized looks on their faces.
He gave an agonized groan.
